newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Murder trial of S.African apartheid assassin begins.
newsitem.headline: Murder trial of S.African apartheid assassin begins.

text.p: Apartheid-era assassin Dirk Coetzee went on trial in South Africa on Wednesday for the 1981 murder of a human rights lawyer.

Coetzee, who commanded a notorious death squad unit to bolster white rule, last year confessed to the murder of Griffiths Mxenge when he applied for amnesty from Archbishp Desmond Tutu's Truth Commission.
But the court trial is going ahead despite a pending decision on Coetzee's application.

Coetzee and his two co-accused Almond Nofomela and David Tshikalanga on Wednesday declined to enter a plea for the slaying of Mxenge, who was stabbed and beaten to death because he handled cases for the then-banned African National Congress (ANC).
In 1989, Nofomela exposed the activities of Coetzee's hit squad, which traced members of banned liberation movements who had infiltrated the country.
When Coetzee defected to President Nelson Mandela's ANC that year in 1989 he began revealing secrets of the dirty war.

Another operative in Coetzee's death squad, Joe Mamasela, who allegedly helped Nofomela and Tshikalanga to kill Mxenge, has turned state witness. He will appear in court early next week to give testimony.
Mamasela said recently that several high-ranking ANC government officials had been informers for the apartheid state. He did not name them.
The commission has refused to hand to the court the relevant video tapes and documents of Mamasela's testimony, given in camera. The matter will be argued in the Durban Supreme Court on Friday.
